Source and artifact scope
https://thehackernews.com/2026/10/russian-apt28-breaches-nato-naval.html
https://www.security.com/threat-intelligence/swallowtail-russia-nato-targets
The source provides exact Edge concealment/task-download commands, wildcard copy to a command script, execution/result upload, and a localhost HttpListener/net-use NTLM capture sketch. The four feed samples reconstruct these documented operations; the fixed challenge and missing script bodies are synthetic, not recovered malware. No sample was executed.
The source supplies no cipher or recovered Events.dat. No speculative decryptor, exploit, family identity, or payload behavior was added.

Placement and matching review
HttpListener construction/configuration remains a neutral HTTP-server operation. The original powershell-httplistener ID now groups New-Object and ::new forms. The old bare powershell-loopback-http-prefix literal is replaced by loopback-httplistener-prefix-add, which requires the actual Prefixes.Add call. The loopback-httplistener composite replaces powershell-loopback-httplistener; both consumers were updated. This narrows URL-only co-occurrences and adds C# without guessing an application context.
HTTP NTLM headers remain notable authentication protocol observations. Header recording remains a notable credential file-write capability; the C# query binds the indexed request header to the file-writing call's second argument. Coercion and capture stay under credential-access/capture/network, with Windows scope because net use WebDAV authentication is the required technique.
The browser navigation matcher accepts multiline command/argv text. The concealment composite requires inline HTML, a tiny window and a far-offscreen position within 1024 bytes. The affected browser observations name Windows, Linux and macOS explicitly. These do not imply command execution without the separate existing copy/execute and upload legs.

Verification
Four feed samples passed the first completed atomscan scan and the final scan. The .cmd has two behavior-based hostile traits plus an existing third-party hostile signature and one suspicious concealment trait. Each NTLM sample has one hostile capture and one suspicious coercion trait.
Nineteen registered fixtures cover New-Object, -TypeName, ::new, direct and piped header recording, C# append/write and multiline arguments, Linux shell continuation, macOS Python argv, missing coercion, missing recording, source comments, wrong data argument, ordinary windows, absent inline content and distant unrelated flags.
Existing browser hostile composite precision scores: 4.8 and 6.1. The NTLM capture composite score is 5.9, above the 3.5 authoring floor.
The source's 21 SHA-256 indicators, 14 distinct malicious endpoints and no package coordinates are recorded in the feed testdata files. Ordinary connectivity probes are excluded from malicious endpoints. Full source extraction, images, command blocks, facts, scan output and reconstruction notes are in scratch/threat-feed/3931 outside its sample directory.

Fixture validator scope
The validate path omits inline YARA by default. The browser fixture explicitly sets enable_yara=true and requires both existing behavior-based hostile composites, in addition to the separate atomscan floor check. No-record coercion controls are in the intent-bearing fixture set because coercing authentication remains suspicious without a file-write sink.
